The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is a key enzyme complex in cellular respiration that converts pyruvate into acetyl CoA, linking glycolysis to the citric acid cycle.  
It is located in the mitochondrial matrix, not the sarcoplasm.  
It does not catalyze the conversion of pyruvate to lactate (that is lactate dehydrogenase under anaerobic conditions) nor lactate to pyruvate.  

Final answer: (B)
